UPI Merchant Discount Rate MDR on Select Person to Merchant Transactions will be implemented
after Diwali.
In a social media post, National Payments Corporation of India said UPI and Services
Steering Committee today decided that keeping in mind the festive season, MDR on Select
person-to-merchant UPI transactions will be implemented immediately post Diwali. Its
other date will be notified separately. All person-to-person UPI transactions will remain
free regardless of amount. The MDR charges will apply only to person-to-merchant transactions
exceeding Rs. 2,000. Around 96% of person-to-merchant UPI transactions will remain unaffected.
Small merchants, including street vendors, receiving up to Rs. 1 lakh per month through
UPI QR codes under the person-to-person merchant category, will continue to enjoy zero MTR on
all transactions.

The International Monetary Fund IMF has raised India's GDP growth forecast to 7% for 2026.27
up from 6.4% in July. In its flagship World Economic Outlook report, IMF said, the revision
in estimate comes on the back of a stronger than expected momentum supported by resilient
domestic demand and robust services activity. It said, India stands out with upward
provisions reflecting sustained momentum and growing evidence of stronger growth potential,
supported by favorable demographic dynamics, expanding domestic market
and continued structural reforms. Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal today hailed the
IMF's projection of 7% GDP growth for India in 2027. The minister said,
the country's multiple free trade agreements pursued under the leadership of Prime Minister
in Modi are expected to boost global economic activity and strengthen supply chain resilience.
Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand will be on a two-day visit to India from today.
During her visit, she will meet external affairs minister Dr S. J. Shankar
and skill development and entrepreneurship minister Jayant Chaudhary tomorrow.
Meanwhile, Canada's High Commissioner to India, Christopher Cooter,
said Canada is looking to strengthen bilateral trade with India through a proposed free trade
agreement, greater investment and increased movement of people between the two countries.

India has operationalized its new resident mission in San Jose, Costa Rica, marking a
significant step towards expanding its diplomatic footprint in Central America.
The mission is expected to further strengthen bilateral relations between India and Costa
Rica. The external affairs ministry said it will also facilitate closer political
political engagement, promote bilateral trade, investment in economic cooperation, and strengthen
cooperation in areas of mutual interest. The ministry said the mission will also provide
enhanced consular assistance to Indian nationals and the Indian community in Costa Rica, and
help protect their interests.
In Punjab, an anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota has been shot dead in broad daylight
allegedly buy a chemist in Mansar today, when he went to the chemist shop to object to him for
allegedly selling drugs. During the argument with the anti-drug activist and his companions,
the chemist opened fire on Parvinder. He received three bullet shots. He was taken to the civil
hospital where the doctors declared him dead. Leaders from various political parties including
the BJP, SAD and Congress have condemned the incident and blamed the state government for
deteriorating low and order situation. In Nepal, more than 100 foreign trekkers are stranded
at various locations after flooding. Over the weekend, swept away hiking trails and
bridges in the country's central region. Authorities rescued 321 people, including
12 foreigners, today after a pre-dawn landslide in Gorka district about 100 km west of Kathmandu.
The Intermetrological Department, IMD, has forecast heavy rainfall over the Andaman
in Iqobar Islands today, IMD said. Heavy rainfall and thunderstorms accompanied by
hailstorm are also likely to prevail over Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh till tomorrow.
